title: Evaluate virtual nodes only for compatible burst workloads
description: Virtual nodes use Azure Container Instances and have different networking, identity, storage, OS, and feature constraints from regular AKS nodes. Verify the current support matrix, cold-start behavior, regional quota, and cost before adopting this burst path.

title: Size nodes against measured workload and failure capacity
description: Choose node sizes and counts using CPU, memory, pod density, network throughput, storage limits, and failure-domain needs. Reserve capacity for system components and upgrades, and benchmark cost and latency rather than optimizing only VM price.

title: Evaluate Arm64 with workload and add-on compatibility tests
description: Benchmark supported Arm64 VM sizes for price/performance. Publish multi-architecture images and verify every sidecar, DaemonSet, driver, and security agent supports the target architecture before scheduling workloads there.

documentation.title: Evaluate Arm64 with workload and add-on compatibility tests

title: Enforce resource quotas for namespaces
description: Plan and apply resource quotas at the namespace level. If pods don't define resource requests and limits, reject the deployment. Monitor resource usage and adjust quotas as needed.
detail: Resource requests and limits are placed in the pod specification. These limits are used by the Kubernetes scheduler at deployment time to find an available node in the cluster. But developers can forget them and thus impact other applications by over-consuming resources of the cluster

title: Namespaces should have LimitRange
description: A LimitRange is a policy to constrain resource allocations (to Pods or Containers) in a namespace. It's useful to ensure that pods don't forget to declare request limits

title: Set measured resource requests and deliberate limits
description: Set CPU and memory requests based on observed demand; requests drive scheduling and autoscaling. Set memory limits to bound risk and choose CPU limits deliberately because throttling can increase latency. Limits do not prevent memory leaks, and containers exceeding memory limits can be OOM-killed.

documentation.title: Set measured resource requests and deliberate limits

title: Define disruption budgets that permit safe maintenance
description: Use policy/v1 PodDisruptionBudgets for replicated workloads and ensure replicas can satisfy them during drains and upgrades. PDBs constrain voluntary evictions, not node failures or every rollout; overly strict budgets can block upgrades and scale-down.

documentation.title: Define disruption budgets that permit safe maintenance

title: Use supported tooling for workload cost allocation
description: Use AKS cost analysis, OpenCost, or an appropriately operated cost-allocation tool to attribute spend to teams and workloads. Account for shared capacity, storage, networking, and monitoring costs; validate labels and allocation assumptions.

title: When required use multi-instance partitioning GPU on AKS Clusters
description: Nvidia's A100 GPU can be divided in up to seven independent instances. Each instance has their own memory and Stream Multiprocessor (SM).

title: If running a Dev/Test cluster use NodePool Start/Stop
description: Your AKS workloads may not need to run continuously, for example a development cluster that has node pools running specific workloads.

documentation.title: Start and stop an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) node pool

title: Use node pool snapshots for configuration reuse, not data backup
description: Node pool snapshots capture supported node pool configuration for reuse. They do not back up application data, Kubernetes resources, or an entire cluster; ensure the referenced Kubernetes version and image remain supported.

documentation.title: Use node pool snapshots for configuration reuse, not data backup

title: Ensure your subscription has enough quota to scale out your nodepools
description: Azure VMs/nodes have quotas per subscription. Ensure that you have planned for these quota and proactively prepare to request for more if needed

documentation.title: Azure subscription and service limits, quotas, and constraints

title: Use scale down mode to delete/deallocate nodes
description: Scale-down Mode allows you to decide whether you would like to delete or deallocate the nodes in your Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster upon scaling down.

documentation.title: Use Scale-down Mode to delete/deallocate nodes

title: Choose cluster autoscaler or node auto-provisioning intentionally
description: Evaluate node auto-provisioning for supported workloads and regions, or configure the cluster autoscaler for explicit node pools. Respect coexistence restrictions, quota, disruption settings, consolidation behavior, and capacity limits; do not enable competing node scalers blindly.

documentation.title: Choose cluster autoscaler or node auto-provisioning intentionally

title: Coordinate HPA, VPA, and KEDA scaling signals
description: Set realistic requests, min/max replicas, stabilization windows, and metric availability. Avoid competing controllers for the same resource signal. Use VPA recommendations or supported update modes deliberately and load-test burst and scale-to-zero behavior.

documentation.title: Coordinate HPA, VPA, and KEDA scaling signals
